howmuch.anomalyTitle: Monthly anomalies with the linear trend
howmuch.anomalyAria: Monthly anomalies of {{name}} at {{place}} with the trend line and its confidence band.
howmuch.intervalTitle: Change per decade with its {{level}}% confidence interval
howmuch.intervalAria: Least-squares change per decade {{ols}} and Sen slope {{sen}} on a number line centred on zero.
howmuch.intervalNote: If a bar crosses the 0 line, the data are also consistent with no change or the opposite direction.
howmuch.total: Over {{first}} to {{last}} ({{years}} years) the trend line amounts to about {{total}}. This is the slope times the period, a linear conversion, not the observed difference between the first and the last year.
howmuch.why: Why per decade? A rate per decade puts records of different length on the same footing.

significant.olsTitle: Linear trend (OLS t-test, lag-1 autocorrelation correction)

agreement.bothSame: The two tests agree: both significant, same direction.
agreement.bothNone: The two tests agree: neither is significant.
agreement.disagree: The two tests disagree. This can happen when a few unusual months dominate, or when the change is not a straight line.
agreement.unknown: The two tests cannot be compared for this series.

significant.agreementBasis: Compared at p < {{alpha}} before FDR; Mann-Kendall here is Hamed-Rao (Seasonal when Hamed-Rao has no p).
significant.notSignificantNote: Not significant does not mean no change: often the record is not long enough yet, or the variation is too large. This record: {{years}} years, {{months}} valid months.
significant.fdr: Multiple testing: q values are Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted across the {{n}} analysed series of the {{family}}, separately for each test.

family.world: world subset (world cities and global mean)

significant.pSource: All p and q values are read from the analysis results file; nothing is re-tested in the browser.

diag.residualTitle: Residuals: monthly anomalies minus the trend line
diag.residualAria: Residuals of {{name}} at {{place}} over time; {{n}} months beyond three robust standard deviations.
diag.residualKey: Dots: months beyond ±3 robust SD (1.4826 × MAD): {{n}}.
diag.acfTitle: Autocorrelation of the residuals, lags 1–24 months
diag.acfAria: Autocorrelation of the residuals at lags 1 to 24 months; lag 1 is {{here}}.
diag.acfKey: Dashed: ±1.96/√n (white noise). Lag 1 in the results file: {{file}}; in this chart: {{here}}.
diag.acfNote: Descriptive only, computed here from the series. The file's lag-1 value pairs adjacent months without a gap (Pearson r); this chart uses the whole-series mean and variance, so the two can differ slightly. Test p values always come from the results file.
diag.rangeAria: Lowest, average and highest value of each calendar month.
diag.annualAria: Mean of each complete year from {{first}} to {{last}}.
diag.annualNote: Does it look like a straight line, a step or a curve?

method.anomaly: Anomaly: each monthly value minus the mean of the same calendar month over all usable years of the series.
method.ols: OLS: least-squares slope of the anomalies on time. Its standard error, t-test and CI use the effective sample size n(1 − r1)/(1 + r1), with r1 the lag-1 autocorrelation of the residuals (Santer et al. 2000).
method.mk: Mann-Kendall: Original assumes independent months; Hamed-Rao corrects the variance for autocorrelation (all lags; known to be lenient); Seasonal compares each calendar month only with itself, on the monthly values. Sen slope: median of pairwise slopes; its CI has no autocorrelation correction.
method.fdr: FDR: Benjamini-Hochberg across all analysed series of one run, separately for each test; q is the adjusted p.
method.missing: Missing values: months flagged missing, partial or low coverage are left out; nothing is gap-filled for the trend tests.
method.cleaning: Flags: outlier_suspect and known_discontinuity months are only marked, not removed; documented steps are drawn as dashed lines.
